editorial.headline: A Café Activity, Open Nationally but Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers on-premises hot and cold drinks in permanent premises—open to foreign ownership nationally, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the provision primarily of drinks—hot or cold—for consumption at the place of business. It applies where the business occupies part or all of a permanent building, whether or not that premises has equipment for preparing and storing the drinks. The emphasis is straightforward: beverages consumed on site are the centre of the activity.

Registration is open across the full business-scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. At the national level, the activity is classified as **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In other words, national treatment permits full foreign ownership for this activity under the cited presidential regulations.

Bali is the material exception. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every recorded scope carries a Low or Medium-Low OSS risk classification; Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for all KBLI activities in those two risk bands. The restriction is therefore not a reduced foreign-ownership percentage or a local-partnership condition. It is a block on PMA registration in Bali.

That produces a clean but consequential distinction. Nationally, the activity is fully open to foreign ownership and available at every listed scale. In Bali, the province’s risk-based moratorium prevails for PMA registration, despite that national openness. A founder considering this activity must therefore separate the national ownership position from the Bali registration outcome: 100% foreign ownership is permitted nationally, while PMA registration in Bali is blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not change the fact that PMA registration for this activity is blocked in Bali.
